elements.name: Resource
elements.definition: An asset owned or controlled by the organisation: people, money, information, know-how.

elements.name: Capability
elements.definition: What the organisation is able to do, independent of how it is done.

elements.name: Value stream
elements.definition: A sequence of stages that creates an overall result for a customer or stakeholder.

elements.name: Course of action
elements.definition: An approach or plan for configuring capabilities and resources to reach a goal.

elements.name: Business actor
elements.definition: A person, team or organisation that performs behaviour.

elements.name: Business role
elements.definition: A responsibility that an actor can be assigned to, such as Environment holder.

elements.name: Business collaboration
elements.definition: Two or more roles working together on shared behaviour.

elements.name: Business interface
elements.definition: A channel through which a business service is offered: portal, desk, API for partners.

elements.name: Business process
elements.definition: Ordered behaviour that produces a defined result, such as Request Deployment.

elements.name: Business function
elements.definition: Behaviour grouped by skill, resource or knowledge, without a required order.

elements.name: Business interaction
elements.definition: Behaviour performed together by a collaboration.

elements.name: Business event
elements.definition: Something that happens and triggers or interrupts behaviour.

elements.name: Business service
elements.definition: Behaviour offered to the environment, defined by its value, not its implementation.

elements.name: Business object
elements.definition: A concept the business works with, such as Reservation or Placement.

elements.name: Contract
elements.definition: A business object holding an agreement, for example a service level.

elements.name: Representation
elements.definition: A perceptible form of a business object: a form, a report, a message.

elements.name: Product
elements.definition: A coherent bundle of services and objects offered as a whole.

elements.name: Application component
elements.definition: A deployable, replaceable part of a software system: a Module, a service.
elements.svg: <rect x="7.5" y="4.5" width="13" height="15"/><rect x="4" y="7.5" width="7" height="3"/><rect x="4" y="13.5" width="7" height="3"/>

elements.name: Application collaboration
elements.definition: Components working together on shared behaviour.

elements.name: Application interface
elements.definition: A point of access to application services: REST API, UI, CLI.

elements.name: Application function
elements.definition: Automated behaviour grouped by what it does, performed by a component.

elements.name: Application interaction
elements.definition: Automated behaviour performed together by an application collaboration.

elements.name: Application process
elements.definition: An ordered sequence of automated behaviour.

elements.name: Application event
elements.definition: A change of state in an application, such as a published integration message.

elements.name: Application service
elements.definition: Automated behaviour exposed to users or other applications.

elements.name: Data object
elements.definition: Data structured for automated processing: a table, a record, a message schema.

elements.name: Node
elements.definition: A computational or physical resource that hosts or runs artifacts.

elements.name: Device
elements.definition: Physical hardware on which software is deployed.

elements.name: System software
elements.definition: Software that provides an environment for other software: OS, database, runtime.

elements.name: Technology collaboration
elements.definition: Nodes working together on shared behaviour.

elements.name: Technology interface
elements.definition: A point of access to technology services: a protocol endpoint, a port.

elements.name: Path
elements.definition: A link between nodes over which they exchange data or material.

elements.name: Communication network
elements.definition: A set of structures that connects nodes for transmission and routing.

elements.name: Technology function
elements.definition: Infrastructure behaviour grouped by what it does.

elements.name: Technology process
elements.definition: An ordered sequence of infrastructure behaviour.

elements.name: Technology interaction
elements.definition: Infrastructure behaviour performed together by nodes.

elements.name: Technology event
elements.definition: A change of state in the infrastructure, such as a rollout completed.

elements.name: Technology service
elements.definition: Infrastructure capability exposed to applications: Git connector, event bus.

elements.name: Artifact
elements.definition: A piece of data produced or used by development or deployment: a file, an image, a descriptor.

elements.name: Equipment
elements.definition: Physical machinery, tools or instruments that create or use material.

elements.name: Facility
elements.definition: A physical structure or environment: a data centre, a plant.

elements.name: Distribution network
elements.definition: A physical network used to transport material or energy.

elements.name: Material
elements.definition: Tangible physical matter or energy.

elements.name: Stakeholder
elements.definition: A role, person or group with interests in the outcome of the architecture.

elements.name: Driver
elements.definition: An internal or external condition that motivates change.

elements.name: Assessment
elements.definition: The result of analysing a driver: a finding, a measurement, a SWOT item.

elements.name: Goal
elements.definition: A high-level statement of intent or direction.

elements.name: Outcome
elements.definition: A measurable end result that has been reached or is targeted.

elements.name: Principle
elements.definition: A statement of intent that applies to every architecture in its scope.
elements.svg: <rect x="5" y="3.5" width="14" height="17"/><path d="M12 7.5v7"/><circle cx="12" cy="17.3" r="1.1" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/>

elements.name: Requirement
elements.definition: A statement of need that the architecture must realise.

elements.name: Constraint
elements.definition: A limitation on how the architecture may be realised.

elements.name: Meaning
elements.definition: The interpretation or knowledge that a concept carries in a given context.

elements.name: Value
elements.definition: The relative worth or importance of a concept for a stakeholder.

elements.name: Work package
elements.definition: A series of actions with a defined result, owner and timeline: a Work item.

elements.name: Deliverable
elements.definition: A precisely defined result of a work package: a document, a release, a contract.

elements.name: Implementation event
elements.definition: A state change in the implementation: a milestone, a go-live.

elements.name: Plateau
elements.definition: A relatively stable state of the architecture: Baseline, Transition, Target.

elements.name: Gap
elements.definition: The difference between two plateaus: what is added, changed or removed.

elements.name: Location
elements.definition: A place or position where elements are located or behaviour happens.

elements.name: Grouping
elements.definition: Any set of elements that belong together; also the folders of the model.

elements.name: And junction
elements.definition: Joins or splits relationships of the same type: all paths apply.

elements.name: Or junction
elements.definition: Joins or splits relationships of the same type: one path applies.

relationships.name: Composition
relationships.definition: The whole is made of the part; the part does not exist without it.

relationships.name: Aggregation
relationships.definition: The whole groups the part; the part may belong to other wholes.

relationships.name: Assignment
relationships.definition: Who or what performs the behaviour, or where an artifact is deployed.

relationships.name: Realization
relationships.definition: A more concrete element implements a more abstract one: SBB realises ABB.

relationships.name: Serving
relationships.definition: An element provides its functionality to another.

relationships.name: Access
relationships.definition: Behaviour reads or writes a passive element.

relationships.name: Influence
relationships.definition: An element affects a motivation element, positively (+) or negatively (−).

relationships.name: Triggering
relationships.definition: A temporal or causal sequence between behaviours.

relationships.name: Flow
relationships.definition: Transfer of information, value or material between behaviours.

relationships.name: Specialization
relationships.definition: An element is a particular kind of another.

relationships.name: Association
relationships.definition: An unspecified link; directed when a half arrow is drawn.

change.label: Changed
change.meaning: Exists in both plateaus with a different realisation.

change.label: Retired
change.meaning: Exists in the baseline only; drawn dashed at 40 % in gap views.

change.label: Unchanged
change.meaning: Exists in both plateaus as is.

components.name: ArchiMate figure
components.purpose: One architecture element drawn in its ArchiMate figure: layer fill, 1 px layer ink, type glyph top-right, name.
anatomy: Container: layer fill, 1 px layer-ink border, shape from the aspect
Glyph: 18 px, layer ink, top-right (in the header band for objects)
Name: Open Sans 600, 13 / 16, centred, two lines max
Optional change chip below the figure (gap views)
states: Hover (clickable figure): primary state layer 6 %, pressed 10 %
Selected / current: 2 px primary ring, 2 px gap
Retired (gap views): 45 % opacity, name struck through, with the Retired chip
rules: The type decides colour, shape and glyph; never pick them separately.

Shapes: active structure square, behaviour rounded, business/data object header band, contract two lines, representation and deliverable wavy bottom, artifact folded corner, product tab, motivation cut corners, value ellipse, grouping dashed.
A clickable figure is a link or a button with the element name as its label; a static figure is role=img.
Never use the layer colour for status: status stays a StatusChip next to the figure.
a11y: Name = element name + type ("Reservation, business object").
Focus ring 2 px primary outside the figure; on clipped shapes it follows the outline.
Retired state also carries the word Retired (chip), never opacity alone.
components.angular: <atb-ax-figure [type]="'business-object'" [name]="…" size="m" [state]="…"> — custom component, no Angular Material equivalent; renders the .ax-box markup.

components.name: Type tile
components.purpose: The type mark before an element name wherever several types are listed: tables, lists, chips, search results.
anatomy: 20 × 20 tile (32 × 32 large), radius-xs 4 (8 large)
Layer fill with a 1 px inset of the layer ink at 35 %
16 px glyph (24 large) in layer ink
states: Static only: the row or chip around it carries hover and selection.
rules: Always followed by the element name; a tile alone is not a label.
One tile per element; DD files and ADRs use the neutral code / document tile.
a11y: aria-hidden; the type name is in the row (column Type) or the tooltip.
components.angular: <atb-ax-tile [type]="…" [large]="false"> or the .ax-tile class inside mat-list items and table cells.

components.name: Change chip
components.purpose: What happens to a building block between two plateaus.
anatomy: 24 px high, radius-xs, label-medium
16 px glyph square: + Δ − =
AIToolbox state containers: success, warning, error, neutral
rules: Shown in gap tables, gap legends, element headers; never inside a figure.
Computed from plateau membership, never typed by hand.
a11y: The glyph is aria-hidden; the word is the name.
components.angular: mat-chip with .dt-chip-success | -warning | -error and the glyph avatar, or <atb-ax-change [change]="…">.

components.name: Plateau track
components.purpose: Which plateaus an element belongs to, in one glance: B · T1 · T.
anatomy: One 24 × 20 cell per plateau, in plateau order
Member: secondary-container fill; absent: dashed outline-variant
rules: Same order everywhere: baseline, transitions, target.
The full plateau name is the cell tooltip.
a11y: aria-label on the track: "In Baseline, Transition 1".

components.name: Relationship line
components.css: SVG markers: composition, aggregation, assignment, realization, serving, access, influence, triggering, flow, specialization, association
components.purpose: An ArchiMate relationship between two figures, with its line style and end markers.
anatomy: 1.6 px line in on-surface (on-surface-variant for association)
Solid, dashed 6/4 or dotted 2/3 by type
Source and target markers by type
Optional label: label-medium on the surface colour
sizes: One stroke width; markers scale with it.
states: Default · Highlighted (selected element's relationships): 2.2 px primary
rules: One relationship type per line; split or merge paths with a junction.
In LikeC4 the same types are relationship kinds with the same markers.
a11y: Diagrams have a text alternative: the Relationships list of the element page.

components.name: Readiness chip
components.purpose: Whether an ARB submission can go to the board.
anatomy: StatusChip: radius-xs, state container, 18 px tile glyph + word
states: Ready for the board (success ✓) · Needs attention (warning !) · Blocked (error ✕)
rules: Blocked: a blocking check fails on the scope, or a required ASD section is missing.
Needs attention: warnings, a pending reviewer, a change request or an open condition.
a11y: The word is the name; the glyph is aria-hidden.

components.name: Check row
components.purpose: One rule of tools/validate.py with its result and the elements that fail it.
anatomy: 20 px status tile
Title (title-small) + id and level (label-medium, on-surface-variant)
Findings: one line each, element name as a link + message
sizes: Full width of its card; rows grouped under label-medium headers (Structure, Traceability, Plateaus & gaps, Ownership & contracts, Decisions).
rules: Blocking checks fail the pull request; warnings are shown to the board.
Each finding links to the element page.
a11y: The status word is in a visually hidden span next to the title.

components.name: ASD section header
components.purpose: Title of one ASD section and where its content comes from.
anatomy: 28 px number square (surface-container-highest)
Title: title-medium
Source badge: From the model (secondary-container) · Written (success) · Too short (warning) · Missing (error)
1 px outline-variant divider under the header
states: From the model · Written · Too short · Missing
rules: Sections built from the model are never edited in the page: change the model.
Missing sections block the submission.
a11y: The header is an h2; the table of contents links move focus to it.

components.name: Reviewer decision
components.purpose: A board member's decision on a submission, recorded as a Checkpoint.
anatomy: StatusChip with glyph + word
states: Approved · Approved with conditions (success) · Changes requested (warning) · Rejected (error) · Pending (info) · Not required (neutral)
rules: Recorded only through the Decision panel (CMD-DECIDE-CHECKPOINT); an agent never records or changes one (INV-12).
Approve is unavailable while blocking checks fail; the reason is shown.
a11y: Disabled actions use aria-disabled and keep a visible reason.
components.angular: mat-chip.dt-chip-* in a mat-table column; actions are mat-flat-button / tonal / stroked.
